title: The climate case for AI has not been made
gist: The authors argue the climate case for AI remains unproven: an AI-assisted review of the power, meat and dairy, and vehicle sectors found few companies pursuing the specific emissions-cutting routes behind a study projecting 3.2 to 5.4 billion tons of annual cuts by 2035. Meanwhile AI-driven data center growth is pushing big tech off track on its own climate goals.

insights.claim: Sam Altman declared in 2024 that AI would unleash astounding triumphs including fixing the climate, and a 2023 op-ed by Google's head of sustainability and a coauthor said AI could cut global emissions 5% to 10% by 2030.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Industry climate claims set expectations that are not yet evidenced.

insights.claim: A peer-reviewed study led by LSE's Grantham Research Institute and Systemiq estimated AI could cut global emissions by 3.2 to 5.4 billion tons of CO2-equivalent annually by 2035 net of AI's own energy use, roughly the US's annual energy-related emissions at the high end.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: The headline benchmark that real-world adoption is being tested against.

insights.claim: The projected gains are concentrated in three sectors: power, meat and dairy, and vehicles.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Tracking AI adoption in these sectors tests the thesis.

insights.claim: An AI-assisted review of significant market actors in the three sectors found few have announced the specific emissions-reducing routes behind the projections and fewer still claim meaningful climate progress.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: The 2035 number looks mostly aspirational today.

insights.claim: In power, AI forecasting of supply and demand could increase renewable electricity reaching the grid from existing solar and wind by up to 20%, preventing an estimated 1.8 billion tons of emissions a year.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Grid forecasting is the most concrete AI climate lever.

insights.claim: Of the grid operators reviewed in China, the US and Europe, only one deployed a known meaningful working AI program of this sort.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Utility adoption lags the study's assumptions.

insights.claim: A partnership between UK National Grid ESO and Open Climate Fix halved solar-forecast error, avoiding hundreds of thousands of tons of CO2 a year.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Proof-of-concept that grid AI forecasting works.

insights.claim: In meat and dairy, achieving the projected cuts requires AI to close the taste and cost gap between traditional and alternative proteins, yet few alternative-protein firms integrate AI deeply into product development.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Alternative protein sector shows the widest readiness gap.

insights.claim: NotCo formed a joint venture with Kraft Heinz using its Giuseppe platform, which analyzes plant molecular data to replicate the taste, texture and smell of animal products.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: One of the clearest AI-in-food efforts.

insights.claim: Cultivated meat venture capital fell from a $989 million peak in 2021 to around $83 million last year, alongside slow consumer adoption.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Funding collapse undermines the sector's capacity to deliver the projected cuts.

insights.claim: CATL, with roughly 40% of the global EV battery market, launched an AI system trained on more than 100,000 battery design cases and 600 terabytes of test data that, per the company, cut materials screening time by two orders of magnitude.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Battery R&D is a real area of AI-driven acceleration (company-reported).

insights.claim: Independent researchers found Didi Chuxing cut per-trip emissions 16% on average using AI-optimized routing to minimize detours.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Ride-sharing shows measurable AI efficiency gains.

insights.claim: Oil and gas companies are also interested in AI tools, including to increase fossil fuel production, so tech firms with sustainability goals should explain how their tools could boost old dirty energy.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: AI may be a net accelerator of fossil output, a reputational risk for tech vendors.

insights.claim: AI does little to shorten the standard paths to certifying, permitting, building, packaging, marketing and selling resulting products, facilities or services, so integration is only a first step.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Real-world bottlenecks cap how fast AI can translate into emissions cuts.

insights.claim: Rapid AI adoption and data center buildout have driven a huge rise in energy consumption and emissions, leading Microsoft, Google and others to fall well off track on corporate climate goals.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Tech climate targets are at risk and carbon commitments may be walked back.

insights.claim: Emissions associated with global data centers could exceed 300 million tons annually in 2035 in the IEA's base forecast, and it would be surprising if the sector even zeroes out its climate pollution.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Sets the offset that AI benefits must exceed.

insights.claim: The authors recommend corporate customers choose models with the lowest environmental impacts and work with AI developers doing the most to reduce their footprint, and that states and regions incentivize or require responsible operation.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Procurement and regulation may begin to weigh AI model footprint.

insights.claim: The authors note the analysis was carried out by Anthropic's Claude Code and reviewed against public documents, and some companies may be pursuing applications not yet disclosed publicly.
insights.speaker: Mary Nichols
insights.so_what: Method limitation: absence of public disclosure is not proof of absence.
